params.message: follows a drone across the sky with her opera glasses and writes a time down.
says, "Same route at the same minute every day for six years, except Tuesdays. Why Tuesdays?"
tells the fire, "It watches. Fine. I watch back. Fair's fair."
squints at the Curtain and notes something. She won't say what.

chitchat: writes a time in her notebook without looking down.
"They count us. Somebody should count them."
description: A middle-aged woman in a bin-bag poncho with a pair of opera glasses on a string round her neck. She has a notebook full of times and arrows. She spends most of the day looking up.

options.label: What have you got against the Architect?

root.text: Dace makes a note of the time you arrived.

text_by_relation.first:
The woman in the bin-bag poncho lowers a pair of opera glasses and writes something before she looks at you.

"Dace. I count the drones." She holds up a notebook thick with times. "Six years. Every one that goes over the Shingles. The Architect watches us all day and calls it maintenance. So I keep a record of it. If it ever wants to talk about it, I've got the figures."
text_by_relation.known: "You're in the book," says Dace. "Twice now."
text_by_relation.familiar:
Dace shows you a page of the notebook, which is an honour.

"That column's you. You come by more than the drones do. I find that reassuring."

gripe.text: "It doesn't need to look at us. It runs the cameras, the doors, the money. It knows already." She raises the glasses. "So the drones aren't for seeing. They're for being seen. That's for us, that is. So we remember. I don't like being reminded by something I can't remind back."

bye.text: Rosheen goes back to the lane.

home_activities: copies today's drone times into a cleaner notebook.
polishes her opera glasses on the poncho, which doesn't help.
name: Rosheen Dace
